gaps.name: The producer census fails when a bracket half is deleted
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the census guards the dispatch, return and --role/--read halves but not the checkpoint arm, so one stated AC5 clause ("dropping any one of its CLOSING events makes the test fail and name the file") does not hold
gaps.evidence: Proved by patch-and-rerun in a scratch copy of the tree: deleting plan.md's line 196 (`--event checkpoint ... --plan cad-planner`) leaves `node --test cadence-core/bin/trace.test.mjs` at 45 pass / 0 fail; deleting ALL FOUR of plan.md's `--event checkpoint` closes (dropping it from 12 to 8 trace-append lines) also leaves 45 pass / 0 fail. cadence-core/bin/trace.test.mjs:740-765 asserts dispatched >= minDispatch, TERMINAL closes >= dispatches and `return` closes >= dispatches, with no symmetric checkpoint assertion - and SUMMARY.md's deviation 1 argues the checkpoint arm is load-bearing (it is the only close on a failed, empty or unparseable return, i.e. exactly the dispatch that burned budget and came back unusable). All six proofs the PLAN named do land verbatim, so this is the uncovered seventh, not a failure of the six.
gaps.missing: Add the symmetric per-file assertion beside the existing two in the BRACKETING loop (trace.test.mjs:740-765): `checkpoint` closes >= dispatches, with expected and actual counts in the failure message. It holds on the tree today at 4/4 for plan.md and 1/1 for the other four bracketing files, so it lands green and closes the hole. SUMMARY.md already files this as a checker warning.

gaps.name: The per-role renderer misbills two reproducible edge inputs
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the roles aggregation loses a whole render block on one role name and credits tokens to a role that never dispatched
gaps.evidence: (a) cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:346 assigns into a plain object literal (`roles: {}` at :275), so `out.roles['__proto__'] = row` sets the prototype instead of an own key; reproduced against a scratch --dir, a `__proto__` dispatch plus a `return --tokens 500` renders with NO `roles` key at all because planning.mjs:2219 gates on Object.keys(r.roles).length. (b) lib/trace.mjs:313-334 sums tokens on `e.role` independently of the (corr, phase, plan) pairing loop and never checks a terminal's role against its dispatch's; reproduced, a bracket opened as cad-executor and closed as cad-reviewer renders {"cad-executor":{dispatches:1,unrecorded:1},"cad-reviewer":{dispatches:0,tokens:500}} - the role that ran reads as unmeasured and a role that never ran carries the bill. A third, not reproduced: `recorded` is incremented per token-bearing event rather than per matched dispatch, so a duplicated terminal could satisfy two dispatches' accounting and hide an unrecorded one. All three are disclosed in SUMMARY.md's Open items; none affects this phase's own trace, where every role name is legitimate and every bracket is role-consistent.
gaps.missing: (a) one line: `roles: Object.create(null)` at lib/trace.mjs:275 (and JSON.stringify still emits it). (b) either validate a terminal's role against its paired dispatch's and report the mismatch, or - cheaper and enough for the record to be readable - never emit a role row whose dispatches is 0 without saying where its tokens came from. (c) count `recorded` per matched dispatch in the pairing loop rather than per token-bearing event.

human_checks.name: Run one full phase through /cad-context, /cad-plan and /cad-execute and read `trace render --phase <N>`'s roles block
human_checks.expected: Every role that ran in the phase appears with a dispatch count, and each closed bracket carries a token figure read off the host's subagent return metadata - no role that actually ran is reported entirely `unrecorded`, and no bracket is left in `unpaired`.
human_checks.why_human: The brackets are PROSE instructions to a model, not code paths. The census proves they are written down and speak the renderer's vocabulary; whether the orchestrator actually runs each one and reads a real figure off the return metadata can only be observed in a live run - and the provenance of a `--tokens` value (real metadata versus a typed number) is not machine-checkable at all.
